title: MATKP Functional Annotations
bodyHtml:
This page focuses on gene expression and potential regulatory regions within adipose tissue. The genetic associations underlying regulatory region-genomic connections are generated by bottom-line integrative meta-analysis of Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) from the Association to Function Knowledge Portal (A2FKP). Transcriptomic and regulatory region annotations are derived from the Common Metabolic Diseases Genome Atlas (CMDGA). Learn more about the Credible Sets to Cell Type (CS2CT) method here.

Explore MATKP to learn more about adipose tissue-relevant datasets, phenotypes, cell type expression, or differential gene expression in various conditions.
dataPoints:
Section,Documentation
Gene expression for Adipose Tissue,"The plot and table display absolute gene expression levels in this tissue (mean transcripts per million) vs. genericity (a measure of tissue specificity; higher values indicate less specificity)."
Credible Sets to Cell Type,"The Credible Sets to Cell Type method (CS2CT) identifies credible set variants that are located within regions annotated as potential regulatory elements in specific tissues. This can suggest which variants, genes, and tissues are important for diseases and traits. The Combined score represents the probability that the SNP overlap with the annotation is tissue-specific. The default view shows credible set variants for the phenotype for which GWAS associations are most enriched within epigenomic annotations. View a different phenotype by typing into the search box. You can view results for different ancestries, where available, for CS2CT and for Global enrichment using the Search by Ancestry menu below."
Global enrichment,"The table displays tissue-specific epigenomic annotation types in which genetic associations for the listed phenotypes are significantly enriched. Use the Search by ancestry menu in the blue bar above to view results for different ancestries, where available."
